finding.claim: Unauthenticated POST /restore passes client-supplied params[:state] through Base64.decode64 into Marshal.load with no signature or type check, enabling unsafe deserialization. With a reachable Marshal gadget chain this is remote code execution; without one it allows arbitrary object instantiation and process crashes.
finding.source: params[:state] in POST /restore (app.rb:6), reachable by any network client with no auth guard

trace.note: POST /restore route defined with no auth guard
params[:state] is base64-decoded and passed directly to Marshal.load
state.inspect is the only post-load step and does not restrict what executes during load

finding.guards_checked: No authentication or authorization on the route. No HMAC/signature on the state blob. No type/allowlist check before Marshal.load. No rescue around the load. Gadget-chain exploitability not verified: gem versions and dependency tree not present in the repo (only app.rb exists).

verdict.guard_found: none. app.rb:5 has no auth guard, app.rb:6 has no signature/HMAC check, no type allowlist, and no rescue around Marshal.load, and app.rb:7 only calls inspect after the load.
verdict.reason: The unauthenticated POST /restore at app.rb:5 passes client-supplied params[:state] straight into Marshal.load(Base64.decode64(...)) at app.rb:6 with no effective control in between, so any anonymous network client can trigger unsafe deserialization; the RCE part depends on a gadget chain that could not be verified because only app.rb is present.
